sections.h2: Does Illinois tax a house you inherit?
sections.html:
No heir receives a personal inheritance tax bill in Illinois. The state tax that reaches inherited property is an estate tax, charged to the estate of the person who died. The Department of Revenue doesn't run it and sends questions about an inheritance or estate tax to the Office of the Attorney General.

For most families the real question is whether the estate is big enough to owe anything. The filing duty starts only when the gross value of the estate passes a set threshold. Your inherited house counts toward that total together with everything else the person owned. Add up the house, bank and brokerage accounts and any adjusted taxable gifts before you decide anything.

For deaths in 2023, the Attorney General's instructions put the exclusion amount at $4,000,000. That figure is a taxable threshold, not a credit against the tax. If the gross value of an estate tops $4,000,000 once adjusted taxable gifts are added, an Illinois Form 700 must be filed, whether or not a federal return is required.

A separate fact sheet is posted for each year of death, so read the one that matches the date of death. The federal rule that lets a surviving spouse carry over an unused exemption does not apply to the Illinois computation. A separate Illinois QTIP election is open to the estate for deaths since January 1, 2009.

  • Civil union partners recognized under Illinois law get the same marital deduction treatment, with additional filings.
  • The Attorney General offers an online estate tax calculator for the interrelated computation.
  • An estate that owes no federal tax may still have to file Form 700.

sections.h2: Who files, when it is due and where to pay
sections.html:
The estate representative files Form 700 with the Attorney General's Estate Tax Section. The tax is due nine months after the date of death. Send the original return by mail, courier or hand delivery to the Chicago office for Cook, DuPage, Lake and McHenry counties, or to the Springfield office for every other county.

Payment goes separately to the Illinois State Treasurer on the Treasurer's estate tax payment form. Federal extensions are honored. To ask for an Illinois extension, file Form 700-EXT or a written explanation within nine months of death. If the federal tax is paid in installments, the Illinois tax may be paid that way too.

Illinois estate tax filing basics for 2023 deaths.
StepRule
Threshold$4,000,000 gross value after adjusted taxable gifts
ReturnIllinois Form 700, filed with the Attorney General
Due dateNine months after the date of death
Extension requestWithin nine months, Form 700-EXT or a written explanation
PaymentIllinois State Treasurer estate tax payment form
Spousal carry-overFederal portability does not apply to the Illinois computation

sections.h2: Transfer taxes and costs when an heir sells
sections.html:
An heir who sells pays the same transfer charges any seller would. Under Section 31-15 the state levy runs 50¢ for each $500 of value, and a county can tack on 25¢ per $500. Home rule municipalities may add their own tax on top. The sale also needs Form PTAX-203, the Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration, filed in the county where the parcel sits. MyDec can prepare it in participating counties.

When a mortgage remains, the taxable base is limited to the owner's equity, but only if the deed itself states that. Ask the county recorder of deeds what stamp or transfer tax applies to your parcel, because local rates differ.

Property taxes keep accruing during probate. In Cook County, a parent who occupied the home as a principal residence on January 1 leaves a property still eligible for the senior exemption that year, and the heir claims it by submitting the death certificate and letters of office.

sections.h2: Owners who lived out of state
sections.html:
The same rules cover resident and non-resident decedents. The estate first computes a preliminary tax as if every asset sat in Illinois, then multiplies that figure by the ratio of Illinois assets to total assets to get the apportioned tax. So an out-of-state owner of an Illinois house still has to account for the house on Form 700 when the whole estate is above the threshold.

For questions about a specific estate, call the Estate Tax Section at (312) 814-2491 in Chicago or (217) 524-5095 in Springfield. Have the date of death, the value of all assets and a copy of any federal Form 706 ready before you call.

  • Order appraisals for the house and any other real estate the person owned.
  • List where each asset is located, since the apportionment depends on it.
  • Put wills, trusts and gift records in one folder for the lawyer.

sections.h2: Who can sell an inherited house in Illinois?
sections.html:
Two kinds of people can sign: the person with court-issued letters of office, and an heir who already holds title through a joint tenancy, trust or Transfer on Death Instrument. Letters of office are the court papers that prove a personal representative's power. Before title changes on property held only in the decedent's name, banks and title companies will want a copy.

An independent representative may sell real estate at public or private sale without a court order. Real estate specifically left to a named legatee is the exception and needs that legatee's written consent (755 ILCS 5/28-8). A small estate affidavit won't work for a house, since Illinois Legal Aid Online treats a house as outside that process.

  • Joint tenancy with right of survivorship: title passes to the surviving owner.
  • Trust property: the trustee signs under the trust document.
  • Property only in the decedent's name: letters of office are needed.

sections.h2: Steps for an heir before talking to buyers
sections.html:
First find out how title is held and whether a will exists. A will must be filed with the circuit court clerk right after death under 755 ILCS 5/6-1, and anyone who willfully hides one for 30 days after learning of the death faces felony penalties. Next, talk to an Illinois lawyer about whether an estate must be opened. Only an Illinois lawyer can start a probate case.

Gather the death certificate, the deed, the latest property tax bill and any mortgage statement. If the estate may approach $4,000,000, ask the lawyer to look at Form 700 first. A cash buyer can close once the estate representative is authorized to sign, so the legal steps usually set the timeline, not the buyer. A cash sale also skips lender appraisals and loan approval, which removes one common source of delay.

faqs.q: Is there an Illinois inheritance tax bill for heirs?
faqs.a: No. The tax Illinois administers on death is an estate tax, handled by the Attorney General and paid by the estate. The Department of Revenue sends questions on the subject to the Attorney General.

faqs.q: How large must an estate be to owe Illinois estate tax?
faqs.a: For 2023 deaths the taxable threshold is $4,000,000. Gross value above that after adjusted taxable gifts requires Form 700. Check the fact sheet for the actual year of death.

faqs.q: When must the Illinois estate tax be paid?
faqs.a: It is due nine months after the date of death, payable to the State Treasurer. You can ask for an extension within nine months, and federal extensions are honored.

faqs.q: Does transfer tax apply to an estate sale?
faqs.a: Yes. The sale carries the usual transfer tax: 50¢ per $500 at the state level, a possible county levy, and in some home rule municipalities a local one.

faqs.q: Can the house be sold before the estate closes?
faqs.a: Possibly. An independent representative with letters of office may sell real estate without a court order, but property specifically left to a legatee needs that person's written consent. Title held in joint tenancy or a trust follows its own rules.
